description: §14.8.9 declassification — reveal("col") is the sole admit path. Wrapping the protected row in u.reveal("passwordHash") at a raw egress (a `_={ … }=` foreign-code block, §23) SUPPRESSES the E-PROTECT-004 fail-closed gate: EVERY protected output column of that query is named by a reveal. The reveal admits the named column past the sink.
rationale: §14.8.9: reveal("col") stamps THE NAMED COLUMN's provenance descriptor as declassified; the sink admits a protected-origin column only when its descriptor bears a reveal stamp. It is the ONLY re-admit path and is greppable in source and emitted handler — so the raw-egress gate that would otherwise fire E-PROTECT-004 is suppressed. ⚑ Read this case WITH its adversarial twin `reveal-wrong-column-e004`, which reveals a DIFFERENT column and correctly still fires: the suppression is COLUMN-keyed, not existence-keyed, and this case alone cannot distinguish the two rules. The case previously used a manual `new Response(...)`; that shape is now E-PROTECT-005, which reveal deliberately does NOT discharge (a hand-serialized Response is not walkable by the floor at all), so the raw-egress limb is exercised here through the foreign block instead. ⚑ S441 (`g-protected-column-escapes-redaction-as-scalar`): `I-PROTECT-STRIP-001` no longer co-fires here, because nothing is stripped — the info now fires only for a query whose row the egress sink ACTUALLY stripped (the §14.8.9 provenance flow, `compiler/src/codegen/protect-flow.ts`). Before S441 it fired for every protected SELECT, and this case pinned that false claim. `E-PROTECT-006` is also silent: `JSON.stringify` of a row whose every protected column is revealed carries nothing protected.
